submission.justification:
Algorithm-L3 (Iterative Topological Clustering with Learned Calibration) at 30 GeV threshold is recommended based on comprehensive simulation evidence demonstrating it achieves the highest possible signal efficiency while satisfying all constraints.

PERFORMANCE: Achieves 93.368% signal efficiency at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate - the maximum of all 22 simulation configurations tested. This represents substantial gains of +7.98 percentage points over Algorithm-L1 (85.39%) and +19.45 percentage points over Algorithm-L2 (73.91%).

THRESHOLD OPTIMIZATION: The 30 GeV threshold was validated through two levels of simulation scans: (1) coarse scan across 20-60 GeV range showing all algorithms peak at 30 GeV, and (2) fine-grained scan from 28-32 GeV definitively confirming 30 GeV as the optimal threshold with a well-defined efficiency maximum.

ROBUSTNESS: The configuration demonstrates operational robustness, maintaining >91% efficiency across ±2 GeV threshold uncertainty (92.37% at 28 GeV, 91.32% at 32 GeV).

ALGORITHMIC SUPERIORITY: Algorithm-L3 systematically outperforms competitors at every tested threshold (20, 30, 40, 50, 60 GeV), demonstrating that its iterative topological clustering approach with learned calibration provides genuine algorithmic advantages rather than threshold-specific optimization.

HARDWARE COMPLIANCE: All hardware deployment requirements are satisfied - the algorithm fits within FPGA resource budgets (LUTs, DSPs), is compatible with 25 Gb/s optical link bandwidth, and is confirmed deployable in Level-1 trigger hardware.

This configuration maximizes physics reach for the new signature search while efficiently utilizing the allocated trigger rate budget.
